To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
six previously reported pathologic mutations in STUB1 (encoding the E3 ligase CHIP) have a profound impact of CHIP protein stability and folding.

the pathogenic STUB mutations E28K, N6S, K145, M211I and S236T and T246M have profound effects on the protein structure and stability of the encoded CHIP proteins, as well as their dimerization ability.

we have studied six pathogenic STUB mutations in the CHIP protein, which is the protein encoded by the STUB1 gene, and we show that some of them affect the protein structure, dimerization, and stability of CHIP in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how mutations in the STUB1 gene, which encodes the ubiquitin E 3 ligase CHIP, lead to a neurodegenerative disorder called Spinocerebell ataxia, Autosomal Recessive 16 ( SCAR16 ).
the characterization of six STUBL1 variants in Spinocerebell ataxia 1.
the in vitro characterization of six different STUB1 variants, known to cause SCAR16, using a combination of biochemical and biophysical methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the disease mechanism behind SCAR16 is related to the loss of CHIP’s chaperone and/or ubiquitin ligase activity, and that this is caused by a loss of CHIP’s structural stability and/or its dimerization capacity, which is dependent on the specific mutation.
SCAR16 is a protein conformation disorder.

these mutations cause the disease by altering CHIP protein structure and stability, thereby leading to impaired E3 ligase activity and/or interaction with chaperones, and eventually resulting in the accumulation of misfolded and/or aggregated proteins in the cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SCAR16 is caused by impaired CHIP function and not by a loss of function.
SCAR16 mutations can be classified as either affecting CHIP dimerization or protein folding.
SCAR16 mutations cause CHIP to become more unstable and less capable of forming functional dimers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pathomechanisms of SCAR16 likely involve a combined effect of impaired chaperone activity and/or E3 ubiquitin-ligase activity, in combination with altered CHIP stability, folding, aggregation propensity, and dimerization.
SCAR16 is a disease caused by CHIP misfolding.
the pathogenic STUB variants affect the structural properties of CHIP, which may lead to a loss of function of the protein.
